statement: Let X, V, Y be smooth integral projective varieties, let π : V → X be birational, and let f : V → Y be surjective with connected fibers. Let D be a reduced effective divisor on X, let c ≥ 0 be an integer, and let L be a line bundle. Suppose that L has a semipositive metric hL with locally bounded weights and that M = −KX + cD has a semipositive singular metric hM . In local coordinates and a compatible frame of M, write dµ = |d|2c e−φM dVX, where d is an equation of D, and assume µ(X) < ∞. Put E = KV/X. Assume that for some integer a > 0 there is a nonzero rational section τ of aπ∗L, regular over a dense base open subset, and that rk f∗OV E + cπ∗ D + paπ∗ L  = 1 for every integer p ≥ 0. (12.1) If dim Y > 0, there are a smooth projective modification Y ′ → Y , a line bundle B on Y ′, a reduced effective divisor D′, and integers d0 > 0, c′ ≥ 0 with the following properties. The line B has a semipositive metric with locally bounded weights. The line −KY ′ + c′D′ has a semipositive metric inducing a finite measure. On a smooth resolution π′ : V ′ → X, f′ : V ′ → Y ′ of the main transform there is a nonzero regular homomorphism (f′ )∗ B −→ d0a(π′ )∗ L, (12.2) and Supp π′ ∗(f′ )∗ D′ ⊆ Supp D. (12.3) Consequently, for every m > 0, a nonzero rational section of mB with poles only on D′ gives a nonzero rational section of md0aL with poles only on D. There is also a smooth invariant version. In that version D = 0, both metrics are smooth, an algebraic torus acts compatibly on X, V and the line bundles, its action on Y is trivial, and τ is invariant. A Zariski dense compact subgroup preserves the metrics. Replace the ranks in (12.1) by the ranks of the invariant parts, still for every p ≥ 0. Then the transferred section on X is invariant and regular. Anticanonical bundles in this version carry their natural linearizations.
